package_info.package_name: polyfill.io (CDN service, as used by npm packages such as create-polyfill-service-url and dynamic-polyfill)
package_info.package_manager: npm (and any web project embedding the CDN)
package_info.package_versions: All versions using cdn.polyfill.io after domain ownership change (February 2024 onward)
package_info.why_malicious: After a change in domain ownership in February 2024, the polyfill.io CDN began serving malicious JavaScript. The CDN injected code that redirected mobile users to attacker-controlled scam sites, impacting any website or npm package embedding scripts from cdn.polyfill.io. This represents a supply chain attack, as the malicious code was automatically delivered to all dependent sites and packages, enabling widespread user redirection, phishing, and potential further compromise.

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, when a user visits a website embedding the CDN script
execution_context.file_location: Served JavaScript from cdn.polyfill.io (injected into web pages via <script src="https://cdn.polyfill.io/v3/polyfill.min.js"></script>)
required_permissions: DOM access (to read window.location and navigator.userAgent)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code inspects the user's browser user agent string to determine if the visitor is on a mobile device, then forcibly redirects the browser to an attacker-controlled scam site, resulting in user redirection and exposure to phishing or fraud.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code performs user agent detection and forcibly redirects users to an external, attacker-controlled domain, which is not expected or legitimate behavior for a polyfill library. This redirection is automatic and targets mobile users, increasing the likelihood of successful phishing or fraud.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A polyfill service is expected to provide compatibility code for older browsers only, without performing user agent checks for malicious redirection or interacting with the DOM in a way that changes navigation. Injecting redirection logic into a widely used CDN script fundamentally violates the trust and purpose of such a service.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: User agent checks and redirection may be used in legitimate contexts for mobile site optimization or A/B testing, but never within a polyfill CDN script, which should be limited to feature detection and polyfill delivery. In this context, such behavior is entirely out of scope and malicious.
key_indicators: User agent sniffing for mobile devices within a polyfill script
Forced redirection to external, attacker-controlled domains from a CDN script
Presence of non-polyfill logic (e.g., window.location manipulation) in a polyfill CDN file
Malicious code injected into all sites using the CDN, not just a single application

attack_chain.action: A website or npm package embeds the polyfill.io CDN script via a <script> tag or dependency.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious JavaScript is loaded into the user's browser from cdn.polyfill.io.

attack_chain.action: The malicious JavaScript executes in the browser context upon page load.
attack_chain.leads_to: The script checks if the visitor is on a mobile device by inspecting the user agent string.

attack_chain.action: If the user is on a mobile device, the script redirects the browser to a scam site controlled by the attacker.
attack_chain.leads_to: The user is exposed to phishing, fraud, or further malware via the scam landing page.

behavioral_signatures: Polyfill CDN script performing user agent checks and conditional redirection logic
Unexpected network requests or browser redirects to domains unrelated to polyfill.io from polyfill scripts
Polyfill scripts containing obfuscated, minified, or non-polyfill logic such as window.location manipulation or DOM-based redirection
file_indicators: Any JavaScript file loaded from cdn.polyfill.io after February 2024
Presence of user agent sniffing and window.location.href assignment in polyfill CDN scripts
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP(S) requests or browser redirects from polyfill scripts to attacker-controlled domains (e.g., scam-landing.example.com or similar scam infrastructure)
Any HTTP(S) requests initiated by polyfill scripts to domains not affiliated with polyfill.io or its legitimate maintainers
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for websites or npm packages loading scripts from cdn.polyfill.io, especially after February 2024. Analyze loaded polyfill scripts for non-standard logic, such as user agent checks and window.location redirects. Use Content Security Policy (CSP) violation reports to detect unexpected script sources or redirections. Flag any polyfill CDN usage after the domain's change of ownership as high risk. Correlate network logs for outbound requests or redirects to non-polyfill domains initiated by polyfill scripts, and inspect for the presence of user agent sniffing and redirection logic within CDN-delivered JavaScript.
